source: Massoudi & Fuge (2025) Agentic LLMs for Conceptual Systems Engineering and Design
finding: A nine-role multi-agent system (MAS) staged as requirements, decomposition, subsystem model and code builds a Design-State Graph for a solar water filter. It is compared with a two-agent Generator-Reflector loop (2AS).
numbers: 60 runs: 2 LLMs (Llama 3.3 70B, DeepSeek R1 70B) x 2 systems x 3 temps x 5 seeds. JSON validity 100% and embodiment tagging 100% in all runs.
limits: One case study; only code that starts was tested (Level 1 of 7); no human designers as baseline.
agent_relevance: Staged roles give the right shape of output but not the content. Our S1/S2 need a code-checked coverage test, not a model claim of completion.

source: Massoudi & Fuge (2025) Agentic LLMs for Conceptual Systems Engineering and Design
finding: Requirement coverage was almost zero even with a full staged pipeline. The staged agents did not carry the requirement list into the design.
numbers: Requirement coverage M2: 0% for all Llama runs; best 20% (R1 + MAS, T=0.0); 2% at T=1.0 for R1 MAS; 0.4% for R1 2AS at T=1.0. The brief had 10 requirements (SR-01..SR-10).
limits: Strict exact-match regex for SR-XX; paraphrased links would not count, so coverage is a lower bound. Authors audited by hand and still saw low coverage.
agent_relevance: Direct warning for S1 (restate problem and requirements): a restatement step must be followed by a program check that every requirement id is traced downstream.

source: Massoudi & Fuge (2025) Agentic LLMs for Conceptual Systems Engineering and Design
finding: More stages gave finer decomposition but cost much more time. The simple loop collapsed to one node.
numbers: DeepSeek R1: MAS 5-6 nodes (6 +/- 1.9 at T=1.0) and about 650 s; 2AS 1-2.8 nodes and 38.6 s at T=0.0. Llama MAS often crashed (over 60,000 tokens or recursion limit), so its runtime looked shorter.
limits: Node count is not quality; authors admit extra nodes may be duplicates.
agent_relevance: Decomposition depth is bought with compute. Cap depth with a counted budget, and count distinct nodes, not nodes.

source: Massoudi & Fuge (2025) Agentic LLMs for Conceptual Systems Engineering and Design
finding: Code from the staged system was less often runnable than from the simple loop, and temperature hurt runnability.
numbers: M4 code executability: Llama MAS 40.2/46.8/49% at T=0/0.5/1; Llama 2AS 62.9/94.7/5%; R1 MAS 34.8/1.3/5%; R1 2AS 100/66/4%. Only R1 flagged runs complete (M5: 2-3 of 5 for MAS, 5 of 5 for 2AS at T=0.0).
limits: Runnable means the script starts with the help flag; says nothing about physics. Large swings at T=1.0 with n=5 seeds.
agent_relevance: Staging alone does not beat a plain generate-and-check loop. Show gains against a two-step baseline, as here. Use low temperature for code slots.

source: Massoudi & Fuge (2025) Agentic LLMs for Conceptual Systems Engineering and Design
finding: The paper gives a seven-level ladder for judging generated engineering code, and measures only Level 1.
numbers: Levels: compile, unit coherence, requirement satisfaction, physics correctness, fidelity, solver-grade quality, lab validation. Suggests pint unit checks and sympy homogeneity tests to reach Level 2.
limits: Authors only propose the checks; they were not run.
agent_relevance: Cheap code-side checks (units, dimensional homogeneity) fit G2/G3: a pass on something the answer was not fitted to.

source: Pradas-Gomez, Brahma, Isaksson (2026) DUCTILE: Agentic LLM Orchestration of Engineering Analysis
finding: DUCTILE splits adaptive orchestration (the LLM agent reads the written design practice and adapts the path) from deterministic execution in verified engineering tools. This puts a documented process into an agent loop.
numbers: Industrial structural analysis at an aerospace maker; 4 input deviations (YAML not JSON, imperial units, renamed nodes, 1.04 force factor). 10 of 10 independent runs passed, with no change to prompt or tools.
limits: One task, 10 runs, 2 engineers; LLM judge (Opus 4.6) plus deterministic comparison; judge output reviewed by an expert with 100% agreement.
agent_relevance: Closest match to our design: model fills slots, program and verified tools decide. Supports G1/G2 and an S1 reading of a written procedure.

source: Pradas-Gomez, Brahma, Isaksson (2026) DUCTILE: Agentic LLM Orchestration of Engineering Analysis
finding: Reliability is framed by pass^k, the chance the agent passes k times in a row. Required repeats come from the Clopper-Pearson bound.
numbers: At 95% confidence: 5 consecutive passes for 0.50 pass probability (S-basis), 29 for 0.90 (B-basis), 299 for 0.99 (A-basis). Their 10 of 10 is below B-basis.
limits: Derived by the authors; their own evidence is 10 runs.
agent_relevance: Use pass^k, not pass@k, when we claim a staged process is reliable. 10 clean runs is weak evidence.

source: Pradas-Gomez, Brahma, Isaksson (2026) DUCTILE: Agentic LLM Orchestration of Engineering Analysis
finding: Authors warn that taking away routine steps leaves engineers with an exhausting supervisory role. The engineer approved a seven-step plan before the agent ran.
numbers: Engineer 1 delegated the whole task; Engineer 2 went one step at a time. Both ended with correct outputs.
limits: Qualitative; two users.
agent_relevance: A plan-then-approve gate (human or program) before execution is a usable S1/S2 exit check.

source: Guo et al. (2025) A Multidisciplinary Design and Optimization (MDO) Agent Driven by LLMs
finding: An LLM agent chains parametric CAD generation, RAG-based concept variants, and tool-driven FEA and optimisation. It follows the staged flow of concept, embodiment and verification.
numbers: Turbine blade: parametric modelling success 80% average, code reduced 83.6% versus manual scripts; FEA workflow about 70% automated; optimisation script success 100%. Machine-tool column: success 75%, code reduced 76.2%. Pass@5 for RAG concept step 80% (blade), 60% (second case).
limits: Three cases, no human-design baseline, success is binary and set by authors; no independent replication.
agent_relevance: Verification stages run by real software (FEA) were where the agent was most reliable. Model-written code is the weak spot, so keep it behind a check.

source: Kumar & Karniadakis (2025) Toward Autonomous Engineering Design: A Knowledge-Guided Multi-Agent Framework
finding: A knowledge-guided multi-agent framework runs fixed stages: kickoff, requirement elicitation, design (sampling, simulation), then review loops. A human Manager ends the loop.
numbers: Demo on 4-digit NACA airfoils, maximise Cl/Cd. Review agent flagged a design with camber 9.2% over the 9% limit and one with thickness 4.59% below the 6% floor though its Cl/Cd was 134.45; another design reached Cl/Cd 206.24 until a new 1-6% camber rule made it invalid.
limits: Single pedagogical case; no benchmark or baseline numbers reported.
agent_relevance: Requirement-versus-output review caught violations that a pure score would miss. Fits G3: check against stated constraints, not the objective alone.

source: de Payrebrune et al. (2024) The impact of AI on engineering design procedures for dynamical systems
finding: Reviews where AI methods fit the VDI 2206 V-model (a VDI 2221 descendant for mechatronics). AI methods are mostly used in early-stage development.
numbers: Authors classify AI methods by V-model stage and give application examples from the DFG SPP 2353 programme; no controlled comparison.
limits: Position paper by many groups; evidence is examples, not trials.
agent_relevance: Confirms there is no controlled evidence that VDI-staged AI beats unstaged AI. Treat stage mapping as a design choice [D].

source: Chiarello et al. (2024) Generative LLMs in engineering design: opportunities and challenges
finding: An NLP count of 15,355 design papers finds where generative LLMs could help across four design phases (problem definition, conceptual, embodiment, detailed).
numbers: 7,034 papers (45.08%) had at least one LLM-like task; Generate 17.88%, Evaluate 42.77%, Describe 18.35%; 12,130 tasks (9,588 unique). Fleiss' kappa 81% (verb class) and 88% (phase).
limits: Text mining of paper abstracts; speculative about benefit; LLM-like verbs are not LLM tests.
agent_relevance: Most design research tasks are evaluation, not generation. Fits our rule that the model fills slots and checks are done by code.

source: Chiarello et al. (2024) Generative LLMs in engineering design: opportunities and challenges
finding: Authors warn that hallucinated, well-formatted LLM output is persuasive and risky for less experienced designers, and call for review of outputs at each phase.
numbers: Qualitative; no measured effect.
limits: Opinion in a framework paper.
agent_relevance: Supports G2/G3: no unchecked model claim moves a stage forward.

source: Ma, Grandi, McComb, Goucher-Lambert (2023) Conceptual Design Generation Using LLMs
finding: GPT-3 concepts for 12 design problems were compared with crowd (Amazon Turk) concepts. Experts rated LLM output more feasible and useful, but less novel.
numbers: 600 solutions rated by 2 trained experts, 0-2 scales, one-way ANOVA; 120 solutions double-rated for agreement (fair-to-moderate kappa). Few-shot output had mean cosine similarity 0.804 (SD 0.06) to the crowd set; zero-shot with a 'unique' adjective 0.746 (SD 0.06).
limits: GPT-3 (2023), not current models; only 2 raters; crowd concepts include off-topic ones.
agent_relevance: Concept generation gives safe but less novel ideas. Novelty needs a different operator or diversity pressure, not stage order.

source: Ma, Grandi, McComb, Goucher-Lambert (2023) Conceptual Design Generation Using LLMs
finding: Prompt tricks traded quality against diversity. Few-shot examples made output closer to human concepts and shrank its spread. Novelty wording alone did not help.
numbers: Convex hull volume: crowd highest; best LLM setting 0.266 (SD 0.1); GPT-3 few-shot and zero-shot-with-novel-adjective gave the lowest volumes. GPT-3 repeated itself after a few outputs when asked for 100.
limits: Embedding-based metrics (MiniLM, 384 dims) are a proxy for novelty.
agent_relevance: Asking one model for many concepts in a single call gives repeats. Use separate calls with different seeds or constraints and measure spread by code.

source: Koh (2023) Using a Large Language Model to generate a Design Structure Matrix
finding: An LLM workflow generated a Design Structure Matrix (system elements and dependencies, a staple of systematic design) and was checked against a published diesel engine DSM.
numbers: Reproduced 357 of 462 published entries (77.3%). Correctness by source text: 82.6% (best), 54.5%, 40.0% for three sources (40% correctness came with 100% completeness); direct ChatGPT gave 66.7%-85.7% correctness.
limits: One engine, one published DSM as reference; source quality drove results.
agent_relevance: Dependency structure can be drafted by the model but needs source grounding and a reference check. Track correctness and completeness separately.

source: Jiang, Li, Qian, Zhang, Luo (2025) AutoTRIZ
finding: AutoTRIZ automates the TRIZ steps with GPT-4 (contradiction, principles, solution report). It uses information entropy over repeated runs as an uncertainty score.
numbers: 10 textbook cases: 7 of 10 matched or half-matched the textbook contradiction within top-3 detections; cases 5-8 showed one dominant answer, others high entropy. Real use case: battery thermal design with 20-30% gain in grouping efficiency and volumetric energy density and over 60% in thermal efficiency, per the authors.
limits: Textbook is the reference though authors say it is not a gold standard; authors judge their own design; GPT-4 only.
agent_relevance: A staged design method turned into a program. Entropy over repeats as a doubt signal matches G1 (doubt only on a signal).

source: Marini & Krus (2026) Context operations to architecture modelling output from LLMs
finding: Proposes formal context operations (policy prompts, persistent reference units, user questions) and an evaluation of model-as-code architecture output against design intent.
numbers: Preprint, Sept 2026; reports utilisation tables for generated architectures; I found no controlled comparison against a human systems engineer.
limits: Skimmed rather than read in full; authors say outputs could be fixed with a few minutes of editing.
agent_relevance: Persistent reference units resemble a stored requirement list carried across stages.

source: Qian et al. (2023) ChatDev: Communicative Agents for Software Development
finding: ChatDev runs the waterfall model (design, coding, code completion, review, testing) as a chat chain of role-playing agents. It is the clearest staged-process LLM system with measured results.
numbers: Averaged over tasks: ChatDev completeness 0.5600, executability 0.8800, consistency 0.8021, quality 0.3953; GPT-Engineer 0.5022/0.3583/0.7887/0.1419; MetaGPT 0.4834/0.4145/0.7601/0.1523.
limits: Authors' own benchmark and metrics; GPT-4 and human judging; software, not mechanical design.
agent_relevance: Staging beat single-step generation on executability by a wide margin (0.88 vs 0.36). Main evidence that a waterfall order helps LLM agents.

source: Qian et al. (2023) ChatDev: Communicative Agents for Software Development
finding: Phase ablation shows each stage adds a different property. Testing drives executability and code completion drives completeness.
numbers: Variants Coding/Complete/Review/Testing: completeness 0.41/0.625/0.575/0.56; executability 0.77/0.74/0.81/0.88; consistency 0.796-0.802; quality 0.2512/0.3690/0.3717/0.3953. Removing all role prompts hurt most.
limits: No confidence intervals given in the table.
agent_relevance: The test stage (real execution) gave the biggest executability gain; keep a run-and-check stage in the schema.

source: Hong et al. (2024) MetaGPT: Meta Programming for a Multi-Agent Collaborative Framework
finding: MetaGPT encodes standard operating procedures (product manager, architect, project manager, engineer, QA) with structured documents between stages.
numbers: Executability 3.75 of 4 on SoftwareDev (70 tasks), 503 s, about 124-126 tokens per line vs ChatDev 248.9; HumanEval Pass@1 85.9 and MBPP 87.7 (GPT-4 setting).
limits: Reported under authors' setup; ChatDev compared on their own tasks.
agent_relevance: Structured intermediate documents between stages halved tokens per line. Pass typed artifacts between stages, not chat.

source: Hong et al. (2024) MetaGPT: Meta Programming for a Multi-Agent Collaborative Framework
finding: Ablation: roles and executable feedback each add value.
numbers: Executable feedback: +4.2 points Pass@1 on HumanEval, +5.4 on MBPP; executability 3.67 to 3.75; human revisions 2.25 to 0.83. Adding roles beyond Engineer consistently improved revisions and executability.
limits: Small differences (3.67 vs 3.75) with unreported variance.
agent_relevance: Real-output feedback beats role-play alone. Supports G2.

source: Qiao et al. (2025) Lang2Morph: Language-Driven Morphological Design of Robotic Hands
finding: Lang2Morph stages a robot-hand design as task to semantic tags to grammar to parameters, then selection and refinement. It is a morphological-analysis style pipeline.
numbers: Diversity score 0.64 (SD 0.13) with diversity guidance versus 0.27 (SD 0.07) without it. Random and direct-LLM baselines used.
limits: Short paper; diversity score is the authors' metric; no physical build comparison in what I read.
agent_relevance: An explicit diversity step in a morphological pipeline more than doubled variety (0.27 to 0.64). Diversity needs a program lever.

source: DRS 2024 paper on LLM-augmented morphological analysis (decompose, generate, combine)
finding: A DRS 2024 paper proposes LLM-augmented morphological analysis split into decomposition, generation and combination stages.
numbers: Not opened; search snippet only. No numbers.
limits: Snippet only.
agent_relevance: Lead for a later pass; check for evaluation numbers.

source: de Payrebrune et al. (2024) The impact of AI on engineering design procedures for dynamical systems
finding: Notes that VDI 2221 and VDI 2206 were created to plan product design for mechatronic systems, and that the V-model originated in software development.
numbers: VDI 2206 (2021) V-model; VDI 2221 (2019) cited as the product design model.
limits: Descriptive; no tests.
agent_relevance: Systematic design and software waterfall/V share roots, so ChatDev-style evidence is the nearest transferable evidence.

source: Massoudi & Fuge (2025) Agentic LLMs for Conceptual Systems Engineering and Design
finding: Human-in-the-loop requirement extraction was bypassed. Each agent got the finished requirements and was forced to emit the FINALIZED token.
numbers: Max completion tokens capped at 60,000; all runs on one GH200 node with vLLM; traces on Zenodo.
limits: The clarify-the-task stage was not tested for models.
agent_relevance: Gap: nobody here tests model quality of the clarify-the-task stage. This is where S1 evidence is missing.
